summary: Filed off a live bench A/B. The user tested the distilled-1.1 int8 (21.5GB) against our shipped fp8 (25.2GB) and reported it better in every way - sound, hands, eyes - and 10 s faster, measured on a 2 s clip at 320x640 (small-clip margin, re-check at a shipping tier). That alone justifies the Balanced swap. The bigger move is the user's: Kijai also publishes the distilled-1.1 delta as a rank-111 LoRA (2.74GB), so ONE dev int8 weight plus that LoRA covers both tiers at runtime - which is precisely what Krea 2 already does with capabilities.turboToggle, the krea2Turbo PromptBox control, Input_is_Turbo (MPI-365) and the Accelerator Lora node's MpiMath gate, and how its separate Turbo card was retired. Ships as ONE card instead of two, 24.25GB instead of ~66GB, and probably kills the variants.arch fp8/mxfp8 split too. The gate is LoRA-on-int8: turbo mode is a bf16 rank-111 LoRA patched onto int8 weights, which is unproven - though the user's runs already carry three baked LoRAs, so if any were live in those generations most of that risk is already retired for free.

Rewritten to the user decision: the distill-LoRA turbo toggle and the dev non-distilled model are DROPPED, so the gate that would have decided the old plan (does a bf16 rank-111 LoRA patch onto int8 weights) is dead - do not re-run it. HIGH stays bf16, BALANCED becomes distilled-1.1 int8_convrot. The card now also absorbs LTX half of MPI-456 because the re-export carries both stages in one 215-node graph, and it picks up media-derived routing (no op booleans), audio INPUT and the transition LoRA. Sequencing consequence recorded: fp8 weights are deleted and the bf16 was never on the drive, so LTX is unrunnable locally and MPI-465 app proof rides on this card rather than preceding it.

Corrected two claims this card made an hour ago after diffing the title sets and reading the app code instead of inferring from names. (1) The export ADDS no inputs - audio input and Input_Use_Transition already ship on both LTX cards, so that acceptance item is deleted, not deferred. (2) The app side is already migrated: commandExecutor.js recognises MpiStageLatents in saveLatentNodeIds and _buildParams already emits Video_Latent.is_continue / .is_preview, because WAN and H3 moved onto that node first. What the export really does is REMOVE seven titles - the two routing booleans, the two stage flags and the four-node latent cluster - all folded into node 568 MpiStageLatents. LTX is simply the last model still on the old eight-node shape, so the remaining work is the generator, the deps and models.js.

Picked up. R2 upload of the int8 transformer started in the background (20.03 GiB, 21505993424 bytes, capped at 3 MB/s per the R2 capability rule so it does not saturate the uplink) and the sha256 is hashing alongside it. Checklist derived from brief.md. Note for whoever reads this next: a parallel session is deprecating WAN text-to-video and will be editing js/data/modelConstants/models.js at the same time as this card - re-read before every write and commit by explicit pathspec.

Implementation complete and committed (92420fad LTX re-wire, 5ab43e4e staging deletion + un-stranding, 6c3762b8 validation + handoff). Card to validating with attention required: every claim so far is static or test-level and NOTHING has run through the app, which is blocked until the app boots and drift-repairs KJNodes. validation.md carries the proved-vs-unproved split; handoff b91a6dcb carries the deliberately-unstarted variants-axis removal.

LTX 2.3 Balanced (int8) now generates END TO END through the app - t2v full, preview, and preview->Continue all pass, which also closes MPI-465. Three defects had to be fixed first and NONE were in the LTX re-wire: (1) muted reroutes in the export severed VAEDecode/CFGGuider links so every output was ignored - mute severs, bypass passes through; (2) workflow-to-api.mjs treated a V3 union widget type (FLOAT,INT) as a socket, emitting nothing AND consuming no positional value, so every later widget on the node shifted by one and node 144 shipped batch_size 24 when 24 was the frame rate - ComfyUI accepts a shifted value silently, which is exactly the plausible-wrong-output failure this card hunts; (3) _inject overwrote the wired MpiStageLatents.latent with the load filename and the node died on a str after four minutes of sampling - fleet-wide, H3 and WAN carry the same node, now pinned by tests/inject-never-clobbers-link.test.cjs. PROGRESS_STAGES re-measured off each run history window: single 3, preview 2, stage2 1 -> 3. A Continue still runs the stage-1 sampler (only the save is gated); the user ACCEPTED that rather than re-authoring the graph, so the count encodes it. Suite 482/482.

R2 upload finished and VERIFIED by effect, not by exit code: rclone reports Multi-thread Copied (new) at 100 percent, the remote listing shows 21505993424 bytes, and a HEAD on https://models.cubric.studio/vision/models/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-1.1_transformer_only_int8_convrot.safetensors returns 200 with Content-Length 21505993424 - byte-exact to the local file whose sha256 is pinned in the dep. Section 1 of the checklist is complete, so a fresh install of the balanced tier now resolves. Everything remaining needs the app: it must boot first so its engine drift-repairs KJNodes 7f43f2c to 35e5956, without which no LTX graph runs at all.

Session close. LTX t2v, preview and preview->Continue all pass through the app on the int8 balanced tier; PROGRESS_STAGES re-measured (single 3, preview 2, stage2 1->3); R2 landed and HEAD-verified. Three fixes shipped that were NOT in the LTX re-wire: the union-widget converter bug, the link-clobbering injection (fleet-wide - H3 and WAN carry the same MpiStageLatents), and the end-frame-only route which was unreachable from the app. That last one needed the graph (H3+WAN re-exported with start.block_if_empty false), the slot gate (stranded-slot bail is now per-media-type) and new UI (the frame-role pill). NEXT SESSION: hard reload, then prove the three i2v routes by their OUTPUT - start-only, end-only, start+end. Commits 78d56890, 890caa0c, c65a1f51.
